questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis with indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are rubbery and non-tender. Dark-field microscopy reveals motile spiral organisms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents as a painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) with non-tender regional lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy showing motile spirochetes (Treponema pallidum) is diagnostic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and erythematous plaques, predominantly affecting the axillae and groin. Nikolsky sign is negative. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid features tense bullae (subepidermal), negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF. It targets BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 antigens.

questions.q: A 40-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden erythema and swelling of existing skin lesions, accompanied by fever and malaise. Nerve function remains intact. What type of leprosy reaction is this?
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction involves upgrading or downgrading of existing lesions with erythema and edema but without new lesion formation. It is a delayed-type hypersensitivity (Type IV) reaction mediated by T cells.

questions.q: A 22-year-old immunocompetent patient presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T4 dermatome, preceded by 3 days of burning pain. The most appropriate antiviral treatment is:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster in immunocompetent adults is treated with valacyclovir 1000 mg TID for 7 days, which achieves higher bioavailability than acyclovir and is the preferred oral agent.

questions.q: A 50-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on the foot with black dots visible on the surface. KOH mount shows copper-penny (Medlar/sclerotic) bodies. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis caused by Fonsecaea pedrosoi (most common agent) presents with verrucous plaques. The pathognomonic finding is sclerotic (Medlar/copper-penny) bodies on histology or KOH mount.

questions.q: A neonate develops a widespread bullous eruption with desquamation within 48 hours of birth. Cultures from the blister fluid are sterile but nasal swab grows Staphylococcus aureus. What is the mechanism of blister formation?
opts: Direct bacterial invasion of the epidermis
questions.exp: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B which specifically cleave desmoglein-1, causing intraepidermal splitting at the granular layer. Blisters are sterile as bacteria remain at the primary focus.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman with a 10-year history of Raynaud's phenomenon develops skin tightening limited to the fingers and face, telangiectasias, and esophageal dysmotility. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is the limited form of systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive in ~70-80% of limited SSc cases.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with pruritic papules on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Skin biopsy shows neutrophilic microabscesses at the dermal papillae tips. Direct immunofluorescence reveals granular IgA deposits at the DEJ. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is characterized by granular IgA at the DEJ and neutrophilic papillary microabscesses. Dapsone provides rapid symptomatic relief; a gluten-free diet is the long-term treatment.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias and a rolled border on the nose. It has been slowly growing for 2 years. Histology shows palisading tumor cells with peripheral retraction artifact. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (nodular type) presents as a pearly nodule with telangiectasias and rolled border. Histology shows palisading basaloid cells with peripheral clefting (retraction artifact). It is the most common skin cancer.

questions.q: A patient with extensive psoriasis is started on methotrexate. Which investigation is most important to monitor for the most serious long-term side effect?
questions.exp: The most serious long-term side effect of methotrexate in dermatology is hepatotoxicity leading to cirrhosis. Liver biopsy (traditionally) or FibroScan (non-invasive) is used to monitor hepatic fibrosis, typically after a cumulative dose of 1.5-3.5 g.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man from rural India presents with painless, progressive destruction of the nasal septum, palate, and upper lip. Biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with plasma cells. PCR is positive for Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis. What is this condition?
questions.exp: Rhinoscleroma is caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis and presents with progressive granulomatous destruction of the upper respiratory tract. Mikulicz cells (foamy macrophages with intracellular bacteria) are pathognomonic on histology.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 = 80 cells/μL) develops multiple violaceous plaques on the lower limbs, palate, and lung. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated red blood cells. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8/KSHV). It is an AIDS-defining illness when CD4 counts are low. Histology shows proliferating spindle cells, slit-like vessels, and hemosiderin deposits.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with recurrent oral ulcers (>3 episodes/year), genital ulcers, and hypopyon uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease is characterized by the triad of recurrent oral aphthae, genital ulcers, and ocular involvement (hypopyon uveitis). A positive pathergy test (pustule formation 48 hours after needle prick) is highly specific.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male with chronic sun exposure presents with a hyperkeratotic, scaly plaque on the lower lip that bleeds on touch. Histology shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with no dermal invasion. This represents:
questions.exp: Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with an intact basement membrane (no dermal invasion). Full-thickness dysplasia without invasion = SCC in situ (Bowen's disease).

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain of the exudate shows Gram-positive cocci in chains. The first-line topical treatment is:
questions.exp: Impetigo most commonly caused by S. aureus (or Streptococcus pyogenes) presents with honey-colored crusts. Topical mupirocin 2% is the first-line treatment for localized impetigo as it is effective against MRSA and has low resistance.

questions.q: A 38-year-old female presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, arthralgia, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive at 1:640 (speckled pattern). Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm antibodies are positive. The most specific antibody for SLE is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibodies are highly specific (~99%) for SLE though not sensitive (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is also specific and correlates with disease activity and nephritis.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery for a basal cell carcinoma, the technique is unique because it:
opts: Examines 100% of peripheral and deep margins via horizontal frozen sections
Only examines the central tumor bulk
questions.exp: Mohs surgery examines 100% of the peripheral and deep surgical margins using horizontal frozen sections, compared to standard excision which samples only vertical bread-loaf sections (~1% of margins). This gives the highest cure rates for BCC/SCC.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man on long-term hydroxychloroquine for discoid lupus develops decreased visual acuity with bull's eye maculopathy on fundoscopy. The mechanism of hydroxychloroquine toxicity is:
opts: Accumulation in melanin-containing retinal pigment epithelium cells
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine binds melanin in the RPE, leading to accumulation and eventual toxicity. Bull's eye maculopathy is the classic pattern. Annual ophthalmologic screening with OCT is recommended after 5 years of use.

questions.q: A 19-year-old immunocompetent patient presents with multiple flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules with central umbilication scattered on the trunk and limbs. The causative virus belongs to which family?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a member of the Poxviridae family. It presents with umbilicated papules and is self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman with chronic venous insufficiency develops a red, painful, edematous area on the lower leg with a sharply demarcated raised border and fever of 38.8°C. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Erysipelas (sharply demarcated border, involves dermis and upper subcutis) is predominantly caused by Group A Streptococcus (S. pyogenes). The sharp border distinguishes it from cellulitis which has indistinct margins.

questions.q: A 26-year-old male presents with anesthesia and loss of sweating in a hypopigmented patch on the forearm. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows lymphocytic infiltration destroying the perineurium with well-formed granulomas. This is consistent with:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with 1-5 well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, negative SSS (low bacillary load), and well-formed granulomas with lymphocytic infiltration and nerve destruction on biopsy.

questions.q: A 33-year-old woman presents with symmetric hyperpigmentation on cheeks, upper lip, and forehead worsening in summer while on oral contraceptives. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation. This indicates:
questions.exp: Wood's lamp (UVA 365 nm) accentuates epidermal pigmentation (appears darker under the lamp) but does NOT enhance dermal pigmentation. This helps classify melasma type and predict treatment response, as epidermal type responds better to topical depigmenting agents.

questions.q: A 52-year-old man presents with a 3 cm pearly plaque with satellite nodules on the scalp. Biopsy shows large round cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and paranuclear whorls of intermediate filaments. CK20 is positive in a perinuclear dot pattern. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a highly aggressive neuroendocrine tumor. CK20 positivity in a perinuclear dot pattern is pathognomonic. CK7 is negative, distinguishing it from metastatic small cell lung carcinoma (CK7+/CK20-).

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless, non-pruritic rash on the palms and soles, along with condylomata lata in the perianal region and mucous patches. RPR is reactive at 1:64. This presentation is consistent with:
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis occurs 4-10 weeks after the primary chancre and features a generalized maculopapular rash characteristically involving palms and soles, condylomata lata, and mucous patches. RPR/VDRL titers are highest at this stage.

questions.q: A 40-year-old atopic patient presents with lichenified, excoriated plaques in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. The predominant T-helper cell subset driving chronic/lichenified atopic dermatitis is:
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis has a biphasic immune response. The acute phase is Th2-dominated (IL-4, IL-13, IL-31). The chronic/lichenified phase shifts toward Th1 (IFN-γ) dominance with increased IFN-γ, IL-12, and GM-CSF.

questions.q: A patient undergoing patch testing shows erythema, induration, and vesicles at the test site at D2 (48 hours) and D4 (96 hours). This reaction represents:
questions.exp: Patch testing detects Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity causing allergic contact dermatitis. Reactions are read at 48 and 96 hours. Erythema, induration, and vesiculation indicate a true allergic reaction (+/++) versus flat erythema alone seen in irritant reactions.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman with psoriasis develops pitting and onycholysis of the fingernails. The nail finding most specific for psoriasis (as opposed to onychomycosis) is:
questions.exp: Nail pitting (punctate depressions from psoriatic matrix involvement) is most specific for psoriasis and is rarely seen in onychomycosis. The salmon/oil drop sign in the nail bed is also highly specific. Onycholysis and subungual hyperkeratosis occur in both conditions.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with skin-colored to yellowish papules in flexural areas along Blaschko's lines. Histology shows calcified, fragmented, and swollen elastic fibers in the mid-dermis. This is associated with mutations in which gene?
questions.exp: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum (PXE) is caused by ABCC6 (MRP6) mutations and affects elastic fibers. Histology shows calcified, fragmented elastic fibers in the mid-dermis. Associated with angioid streaks, cardiovascular, and GI complications.

questions.q: A 68-year-old farmer presents with a rapidly growing then regressing nodule on the dorsum of the hand with a central keratin-filled crater. Histology shows a symmetric cup-shaped squamous proliferation with overhanging epidermal lips and well-differentiated keratinocytes. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma presents as a rapidly growing then spontaneously regressing nodule with a central keratin crater on sun-exposed areas. Histology shows a symmetric, well-differentiated cup-shaped squamous proliferation with overhanging epidermal lips.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male presents with painful genital ulcers with soft, undermined edges and a purulent base. Gram stain shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in a 'school of fish' arrangement. The WHO-recommended treatment is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Chancroid caused by Haemophilus ducreyi presents with painful soft ulcers and 'school of fish' Gram-stain appearance. WHO-recommended treatment is azithromycin 1 g single dose or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM. Azithromycin is preferred for oral single-dose convenience.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with extensive tinea capitis with a boggy, tender, pustular mass on the scalp with broken-off hair stumps. She has cervical lymphadenopathy. This clinical entity is called:
questions.exp: Kerion celsi is a severe inflammatory form of tinea capitis (commonly caused by T. verrucosum or T. mentagrophytes from zoophilic dermatophytes), presenting as a boggy, tender, pustular plaques with broken hairs and regional lymphadenopathy. It represents a hypersensitivity reaction to the fungus.
